I buy everything with my own money. Every item below has been carried, slept in, or hauled up something steep for at least three weeks before I wrote about it, and the notes were taken on-trail, not from the spec sheet. Most gear reviews are rewritten press releases; these are field notes from a desk that has seen real rain.

Trailwright Kiln 38 pack review — eight months, four trips, one verdict

September 2026 9 min read

The Kiln 38 has carried everything from a week of summer gear to a slam-dunk weekend load, and the frame has not once complained. The hip belt pockets are genuinely usable, the load lifter works, and the price is fair for what survives. After eight months and four trips, I think it is worth the extra money.

Solstice Ridge 2P tent review — dry in the rain it was not built for

July 2026 11 min read

Two pounds twelve ounces for a two-person tent is heavy by modern standards, but the Solstice Ridge has something lighter tents lack: a fly that actually reaches the ground. A three-day squall in the high country left the inner tent dry, which is more than I can say for the expensive ultralight I used the year before. For car camping and short backpacks, it is worth the extra money.

Meridian half-zip fleece review — the one I keep reaching for

May 2026 7 min read

Half the fleeces on the market pill within a season or sit there looking sad in a drawer. The Meridian has been washed a dozen times, worn under a shell on ridge lines and over a base layer around camp, and it still looks like the day it arrived. At $58 it is not cheap, but it is the one I reach for every single trip. For most people that means it is worth the extra money.
